from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Define colors for lecture lines
        colors = ["#FF7F50", "#87CEFA", "#90EE90"]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.lecture[0].set_color(colors[0])
        v1 = Vector([1, 0.5], color=YELLOW)

        self.place_at_grid(v2, "C2", scale_factor=1)
        self.play(FadeIn(v1), FadeIn(v2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Span is the total reachable territory.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(colors[1])
        span_area = Rectangle(width=4, height=3, fill_opacity=0.3, color=BLUE, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(span_area, "B3", "E5", scale_factor=1)
        self.play(FadeIn(span_area))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.lecture[2].set_color(colors[2])
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.2}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(grid, "D4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(grid))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Redundancy Test: Linear Dependence", [
            "Linear dependence means redundant, wasteful vectors.",
            "One vector can be formed by others.",
            "Example: A third vector adds no reach."
        ])

        # Define vectors
        v1 = Vector(RIGHT, color=BLUE)
        v3 = Vector(1.5 * RIGHT, color=GREEN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(v1))
        self.play(Create(v3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF5555"))
        label = MathTex(r"v_3 = c_1 v_1", color="#FF5555")
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'B4')
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        redundant = Text("Redundant", color=RED, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(redundant, 'B2')
        self.play(Write(redundant))
        self.play(FadeOut(v3), FadeOut(label), FadeOut(redundant))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Combinations to Bases

sections.title: The Ingredients: Linear Combinations and Span
sections.content: Define a linear combination as scaling vectors and adding them together. Visualize 'Span' as the total reachable space (the 'territory') covered by these vectors. Prerequisite: Students must understand vector addition and scalar multiplication.
sections.example: Imagine a robot at (0,0). With vector v1=(1,0) and v2=(0,1), the robot can reach any point in the 2D plane by combining steps: c1*v1 + c2*v2. The 'Span' is the entire 2D coordinate system.

sections.title: The Redundancy Test: Linear Dependence
sections.content: Explain linear dependence as a 'wasteful' vector. If one vector can be formed by a combination of the others, it provides no new 'territory.' Graphically, this means vectors lie on the same line or plane.
sections.example: If you have a robot with arms pointing at (1,0), (0,1), and (1,1), the third arm is redundant because it's just the sum of the first two. It adds no new reach to the robot's capabilities.

sections.title: The Efficiency Expert: Bases
sections.content: Introduce the Basis as the 'minimal set' of vectors required to span a space. It must be linearly independent and span the space. Think of it as the most efficient instruction manual to describe any point in a space.
sections.example: To describe any position in a 3D room, you only need 3 specific vectors (the x, y, z axes). These 3 vectors form a basis. Adding a 4th vector would make the description 'dependent' and unnecessarily complex.

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
sections.content: Quick recap: Linear combination (the action), Span (the reach), Dependence (the overlap), and Basis (the minimal toolset).
sections.example: Imagine a toolkit: 'Span' is all the things you can fix; 'Basis' is the minimum set of tools you need to fix everything without carrying extra weight.
